title: 5.1.2 Falling Block — Worked Example
description: A dynamic block falls under gravity and lands on a static floor. Read the example, then experiment.

steps.title: Read the worked example
steps.instructions: The starter code is a full working sketch — a block falls and lands on a floor. Click Run to see it.
hints: Static sprites don't move; they push back on dynamic ones.

steps.title: Turn gravity off
steps.instructions: Change `world.gravity.y = 10` to `world.gravity.y = 0` and run again. The block floats.
hints: Gravity units are roughly pixels per second².

steps.title: Change the floor to dynamic
steps.instructions: Remove the `'static'` argument from the ground sprite. Run. Both pieces fall now — that's why the floor is static.
hints: new Sprite(x, y, w, h) defaults to dynamic. Add 'static' to anchor it.

steps.title: Add a second falling block
steps.instructions: Declare another sprite and color it differently. Watch them stack.
hints: Give them different x positions so they don't spawn on top of each other.

requirements.title: Sets world gravity
requirements.description: Assign a value to world.gravity.y or world.gravity.x

requirements.title: Uses a static sprite
requirements.description: Create at least one sprite with the 'static' collider type

requirements.title: Uses a dynamic sprite
requirements.description: Create at least one dynamic sprite (no 'static' argument)
